issues.legal_issue: When the original document is in the possession or power of the opposing party and is not produced after notice, any secondary evidence of its contents is admissible even if the document is one for which a certified copy may be given in evidence.
material_facts: The opposing party had produced the original deed to a public body, along with a plain copy and an English translation, and endorsed that the copy corresponded to the original.
The original was returned to that party, while the copy and translation were retained by the public body.
At trial, the opposing party did not produce the original despite receiving notice to do so.
No copy of the deed could be traced in the registration office, and the party relying on the deed tendered the retained copy and translation.
Admissions by the opposing party and earlier officeholders, together with other evidence, supported the existence of the deed and the dedication of the properties.
issues.conclusion: The plain copy was admissible as secondary evidence because the conditions for admission based on the opposing party’s failure to produce the original after notice were satisfied. That rule was not displaced by the possibility that the document also fell within the category for which a certified copy could be given in evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 65(a) and 66 of the Evidence Act, when the original is shown or appears to be in the possession or power of the opposing party and that party does not produce it after the required notice, any secondary evidence of its contents is admissible. Section 65(f) does not control or restrict section 65(a) when both apply. The Court approved In the Matter of a Collision between the Ava and the Brenhilda (1879) I.L.R. 5 Cal. 568, which held that any secondary evidence may be received where the case falls within clauses (a) or (c), even if clause (f) also applies.

rule.if: secondary_evidence_admissibility_dispute and original_in_opponent_possession_or_power and notice_given and original_not_produced_after_notice and offered_evidence_is_secondary and document_in_certified_copy_category

predicates.secondary_evidence_admissibility_dispute: The proceeding presents a dispute about whether evidence other than an original document may be admitted to prove its contents.
predicates.original_in_opponent_possession_or_power: The original document was shown or appeared to be in the possession or power of the opposing party.
predicates.notice_given: The party seeking to prove the document gave the opposing party notice to produce the original.
predicates.original_not_produced_after_notice: The opposing party did not produce the original after receiving notice.
predicates.offered_evidence_is_secondary: The party seeking to prove the document offered evidence other than the original to establish its contents.
predicates.document_in_certified_copy_category: The document is of a kind for which a certified copy may be given in evidence.

issues.definition: When a secondary-evidence dispute concerns an original document held by the opposing party, and that party fails to produce it after notice, any offered secondary evidence is admissible even if the document is of a kind for which a certified copy may be given in evidence.
